event.name: Search Central Live Deep Dive Europe 2026

sessions.title: Welcome and opening keynotes
sessions.note: Covers two agenda slots: the 11:00 Welcome (event host) and the 11:20 Opening keynote by Lino Cattaruzzi, named in the host's on-stage hand-over; he also presented the Larry Page quote and the five ecosystem principles. Transcript from a second attendee recording; an audio recording covers the keynote from its first minute to the end.

sessions.title: What's new in the world of Search
sessions.note: Speaker from his self-introduction at the start of the talk, in a second attendee recording.

sessions.title: How Search works and where's AI?
sessions.note: Cherry Prommawin presented crawling, indexing and serving in classic Search and Gary Illyes the AI parts (his hand-over and her self-introduction at the start). Transcript from a second attendee recording.

sessions.title: Lightning session A: Automation and AI
sessions.note: Hosted by Gary Illyes and Cherry Prommawin. Seven talks: AI automation in agency SEO work (James Powley, SEO Director, Blue Array: self-introduction and hand-over); LLM errors on search data (Rafael Kovashikawa, AI Engineer & SEO Specialist, FUSE: hand-over 'Raphael', the only Rafael on the official speaker list); an LLM fix loop for structured data (a live demo with Google's Rich Results Test); automating monthly SEO reports (Kira Breuer, SEO Manager, Greven Medien GmbH & Co. KG: hand-over 'Kiran' in the speech-to-text and her self-description as an SEO manager at a local agency in Cologne, matched to the only Kira on the official speaker list, whose job and city agree); preparing sites for humans and AI agents (Carlos Ortega, Freelance SEO Consultant: the next speaker's back-reference 'as we were just shown by Carlos', the only Carlos on the official speaker list); GEO and its metrics (Thiago Pojda, SEO Director & Entrepreneur, SIXT SE: the host's hand-over and his self-introduction); AI search as a funnel. The other speakers were not named. Transcript from a second attendee recording and an audio recording; no slides photographed.

sessions.title: How crawling works
sessions.note: Speakers from on-stage hand-overs between the two and the host's thanks to Gary and Cherry. Transcript from a second attendee recording; two audio recordings cover the talk except for about three minutes before the crawling infrastructure part.

sessions.title: How crawling errors affect Search
sessions.note: Cherry Prommawin presented the status codes and Gary Illyes the DNS, network, CDN and soft 404 errors (on-stage hand-overs; the host thanked both). Transcript from a second attendee recording and a complete audio recording.

sessions.title: How Google interprets robots.txt
sessions.note: Audio recording from the first minutes of the talk to its end, including a robots.txt quiz; the speaker is not named in the recording. The unknown-line slide stays with this talk: the recording reads out its example and value, although the photo's time stamp falls a few minutes after the hand-over to Lightning session B.

sessions.title: Lightning session B: Robots.txt
sessions.note: One community talk was recorded: robots.txt pitfalls seen in the wild (Dave Smart, Tech SEO, Tame the Bots: the host's hand-over, his self-introduction and the official speaker list). The audio recording ends during his talk.

sessions.title: What would you do?: Crawling Edition
How Google thinks about crawl budget
sessions.note: The second attendee recording starts mid-talk, so the opening is from slides only.

sessions.title: Lightning session C: Crawling
sessions.note: Two community talks were recorded: similar URLs (Tobias Schwarz, CTO and Founder, Audisto, from his self-introduction) and why technical SEO still matters in AI search (Jovana Avramovic, SEO Consultant: hand-over 'Joanna' in the speech-to-text, matched to the official speaker list). Transcript from a second attendee recording.

sessions.title: Q&A
sessions.note: Panel named in the moderator's invitation ('John and Gary'); an answer carries a name only where an on-stage cue names its speaker. Audience questioners are not named. Transcript from a second attendee recording; two audio recordings cover most of the panel as well (from the AI crawlers question to the llms.txt answers, and from the Search Console API answer to the end).

sessions.title: Daily wrap-up
sessions.note: Housekeeping only (second attendee recording); no claims.

sessions.title: Day 1, session not recorded
sessions.note: Points from my notes where I did not write down which session they came from.

sessions.title: Welcome to indexing day!
sessions.note: Presented by Gary Illyes and Cherry Prommawin (named in the host's hand-over; turns not attributable). Highly rated Slido questions skipped on Day 1 for lack of time: four on slides with written answers, one more (sloppy migrations) only spoken, then a recap of Day 1. Transcript from a second attendee recording.

sessions.title: How is HTML interpreted
sessions.note: Speaker from a back-reference in a later talk ('Cherry already talked about the page ... main content'), heard in a second attendee recording. The author's recording starts mid-talk, so the opening is from slides only.

sessions.title: Controlling indexing
sessions.note: Named on the title slide. The first recording stops mid-sentence at the closing slide; a second, independent recording covers the end of the talk (robots.txt and robots meta rules, robots meta tags and JavaScript).

sessions.title: Lightning session D: Rendering and JavaScript
sessions.note: Four parts: a short Google opener by Erin Sparling (Partner Technology Manager, Google), then community talks by Sören Bendig (CEO, Audisto) on rendering blind spots, Rebecca Yu (SEO Manager, JAKALA) on debugging JavaScript rendering, and Natalia Venditto (Principal Software Engineer, Adobe) on Web Fragments.

sessions.title: What is Google friendly JavaScript
sessions.note: Same speaker as the opener of Lightning session D.

sessions.title: Understanding what's on a page
sessions.note: Speaker from the author's recording label. Opened with Slido quiz questions, then the part on main content, which only a second attendee recording captured.

sessions.title: Handling web duplication
sessions.note: Speaker from the next talk's back-reference ('pick up where John left off with the canonical links'), heard in a second attendee recording.

sessions.title: Lightning session E: Managing Duplicates and Site Moves
sessions.note: Three community talks: broken canonical graphs (Tobias Schwarz, CTO and Founder, Audisto); consolidating two competing loan-comparison sites into one brand (Martyna Ağanoğlu, SEO Specialist, Loando / Clar); the decisions behind a multi-site migration after an acquisition (David Carrasco Pamies, SEO Consultant, Magnify). Speakers from on-stage introductions and the official speaker list; talks 2 and 3 are only in the second attendee recording.

sessions.title: Finding the gold nuggets: structured data, media, and more!
sessions.note: Short introduction to feature extraction (structured data, images, video). Introduced by name by the host and named again in the hand-over at the end of the next talk.

sessions.title: What is Structured Data and why we need it on the internet.
sessions.note: Named in the previous speaker's hand-over ('Ryan is going to talk about how we are actually dealing with structured data'), heard clearly in a second attendee recording; he said he has been a software engineer at Google for about 15 years, focused on data ingestion.

sessions.title: Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos
sessions.note: Introduced by name by the previous speaker. The author's recording stops partway through the list of video SEO factors; a second attendee recording covers the rest of the talk (video factors, formats, discovery, robots controls, AI-generated images).

sessions.title: Lightning session F: Media
sessions.note: Two community talks, captured by a second attendee recording: rewriting image alt text with an LLM through a crawler (speaker not named) and 'prompt journalism' (Patrick Domanico, Technical SEO Manager & Freelance Journalist, dentsu: hand-over 'Patrick', the only Patrick on the official speaker list).

sessions.title: Lightning session G: Internationalisation
sessions.note: Alizée Baudez (International SEO Consultant) on language, region and authority, named from her self-introduction, which matches the official speaker list; then Zahra Laleh's talk on non-Latin scripts, presented on her behalf by a colleague who was not named; a second attendee recording covers the rest of that talk.

Speakers from on-stage references: a later talk called the first part John's talk, and the first part ended by handing over to Gary.
